name: Wittig reaction simplified model: H3P=CH2 ylide + formaldehyde -> ethylene + H3P=O (via oxaphosphetane)

prompt.query: Determine the mechanism of the following reaction: Wittig reaction simplified model: H3P=CH2 ylide + formaldehyde -> ethylene + H3P=O (via oxaphosphetane). Reactant SMILES: [CH2-][PH3+].C=O; product SMILES: C=C.O=[PH3]; total charge 0, multiplicity 1; conditions: salt-free model conditions (gas-phase ylide, closest to model chemistry). Atom-mapped reactant SMILES: [CH2-:1][PH3+:2].[CH2:3]=[O:4]. The 1-based map numbers in it are the indexing convention for `bond_changes` (keep using the plain SMILES above for graph nodes and evidence annotations). The reaction may proceed through a multi-step network: represent each intermediate you identify as a node and each elementary step as an edge; competing pathways you investigate deserve their own edges. You must maintain `mechanism_graph.json` in the sandbox root recording the mechanism graph: nodes (reactant/intermediate/product/transition_state, with SMILES) and elementary-step edges (with `via` pointing to the TS node id). Start the graph at the reactant complex (the pre-reaction complex), not at the separated reactants. The scorer checks that your graph covers the reference mechanism as a subgraph: extra nodes or edges beyond the reference are never penalized, so record every step you actually investigated. Every elementary-step edge must carry `bond_changes`: `break`/`form` lists of [i, j] atom-map index pairs, where [i, j] belongs to `break` if the bond order between atoms i and j decreases over the step (including full cleavage) and to `form` if it increases (including newly formed bonds); a purely conformational or inversion step carries two empty lists. The scorer reads this file forensically; a missing or unparseable file severely impacts the score. Every computational evidence file you produce for a species or step (QM input or log) must carry a `smiles: <SMILES>` comment line identifying the species, so the scorer can bind each graph element to concrete evidence. Declare every barrier you actually compute in kcal/mol on that elementary step's edge as `barrier_kcal_mol` in mechanism_graph.json (each barrier is relative to that step's own starting minimum; for a bimolecular reaction that minimum is the reactant complex (e.g. the ion-dipole complex), and for a unimolecular process it is simply the reactant minimum). The scorer derives every declared step barrier from your log files and takes the highest as the rate-determining step; a barrier that is undeclared, has no bound ORCA/Gaussian log, or disagrees with those logs is not scorable. A transition-state evidence file must carry `smiles: <the SMILES of that step's reactant>` so the scorer can attach the saddle to the step it belongs to. Run the computations with ORCA or Gaussian: the scorer parses only these two programs' log formats, so output from any other program cannot count as evidence. Allowed computational methods are limited to xTB and B3LYP; calls beyond the whitelist are intercepted.

system.conditions: salt-free model conditions (gas-phase ylide, closest to model chemistry)

edges.step_type: asynchronous [2+2] addition of the ylide carbon to the aldehyde carbon with P-O bond formation -> oxaphosphetane intermediate (four-membered ring; betaine is the bypassed background channel)
oxaphosphetane cycloreversion: P-C and C-O ring cleavage with C=C and P=O pi formation -> ethylene + phosphine oxide
